data.name: Benazir
data.gender_notes: Benazir is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Son of the Lion. Benazir is a noble and strong name with the themes of leadership and courage. It is derived from the Urdu and Arabic languages and is of Islamic origin. The name is often associated with Benazir Bhutto, the first female prime minister of Pakistan. The name Benazir carries the meaning “Son of the Lion” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Urdu, Arabic. Parents who choose Benazir usually hope their child will grow to embody son of the lion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Benazir represents the spiritual strength and courage that one possesses to overcome challenges and lead others.
data.etymology: Benazir belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Son of the Lion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Benazir total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

Benazir Bhutto was a trailblazer, defying societal norms and shattering glass ceilings as the first female Prime Minister. The name has become synonymous with strength and determination, inspiring generations to aspire to leadership and break through barriers.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual sense, Benazir can be seen as a reminder of the courage and tenacity of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). He faced numerous challenges and adversities throughout his life but never wavered in his faith or beliefs. The name Benazir, translating to 'son of the lion,' can be seen as a call to have the courage and determination of a lion in our daily lives, facing challenges with faith and strength. Additionally, in Muslim communities, the name can evoke images of courageous figures from Islamic history, serving as a reminder of the rich history and resilience of the faith.
